You are a senior engineer. Repo /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony (FastAPI src/ask_soony, React web/, uv, ruff line-length 100, pytest). Read AGENTS.md and docs/challenge.md §5-§8 first. Do NOT commit or push. Never print secrets (.env). No paid LLM calls. Never send real messages (email/Teams/push/calls) in tests or checks: mock senders. Never approve/escalate/dismiss real cards. Portal data in data/portal is confidential: only short identifiers in reports.

CONTEXT: Step 4 "Track" at the customer is a hand-kept list, soony/erp/open_shipments.csv, updated "when someone remembers" from carrier emails, supplier shipping advices, portal look-ups and calls. In the current data the whole list has not changed since 20 Nov 17:00 (~37 h), and at least 3 shipments are still "booked"/"in transit" although Hamburg already booked their goods receipts (goods_receipts_update.csv, e.g. GR 5000413067/68/70/71). Our silence check is wrong: api.py ~line 1193 `ref = max(upds)` and shipment_view() measure silence relative to the NEWEST update in the list, so a frozen list looks fresh (same idea in routines.py silent_shipments docstring and launch_view.py ~57). Lio's own example in the brief: "something stops changing ... no news isn't good news".

GOAL: one reconciled truth per shipment, derived from every source, instead of trusting the list. New module src/ask_soony/tracking.py (pure functions + tests), then minimal, localized integration.
1. Evidence per shipment (each a claim: source, what it says (status/qty/date), at, anchor/file+row): the tracker row (status, eta, updated_at, note); goods receipts for its PO numbers/lines (=> received, qty, date, delivery note); supplier documents already parsed by papercheck (shipping advices / ASN / delays: look at how papercheck Doc/claims and verifier dispatch.json `arriving`/`not_counted` reference shipments, AWB, containers); supplier email replies tied to cards (replies.py state); site answers from the "ask the site" feature another engineer is building now (data/state/floor_counts.json or similar, kind "received"; read it defensively if present).
2. Derived status by precedence (receipt > site answer > supplier document/reply > tracker), with as_of and the deciding source. Statuses: planned/booked, departed, in_transit, at_port, delayed, arrived_not_booked, received (full/partial with qty), unknown. Contradictions listed explicitly ("Tracker: in transit (20 Nov); Hamburg booked GR 5000413067 on 21 Nov") instead of silently picking one.
3. Silence against the CLOCK: last_heard = newest timestamp across ALL sources for that shipment; silent_hours = now - last_heard. Feed freeze: list_age = now - newest updated_at in the tracker; if >= ASK_TRACKER_STALE_HOURS (default 12) and the list contradicts other sources, that is ONE finding ("The shipment list has not changed for 37 h; 3 shipments in it are already received"), not 25 alarms. Per-shipment silence alerts only for shipments that are not received, matter for the launch (their parts are short / runs_dry in launch_view or ETA before launch) and have no fresher source.
4. Cards on Today (follow existing card structure; see how api.build_cards / papercheck cards / dispatch cards are built, options, approve path, routine_type, so voice, routines, activity keep working): (a) feed-freeze card, recommended option: ask each affected supplier/forwarder for the status of their open shipments in one email each (use existing ask_status/email option mechanics; free, routine-able), alternative: tell the list owner (the buyer) which rows are outdated (internal note); (b) per-shipment "silent and needed" card: ask supplier/forwarder for status (free, routine-able), if ETA passed and site might have it: ask the site "did it arrive?" (the other engineer's site question kind "received"; if its API is not there yet, leave a clear TODO hook and test the rest). Every card sentence says why it matters in copies/time.
5. Integration (minimal, re-read files right before editing; another engineer is editing api.py, launch_view.py, routines.py, basic_auth.py, push.py, teams.py, cardtools.py concurrently, so keep edits small and localized, never reformat whole files, never revert their changes): shipment_view/launch_view/map use the derived status + clock-based silence; routines.silent_shipments uses the new silence; /api/state per shipment gets `derived` {status, as_of, source, contradictions, last_heard, silent_hours} and a top-level `tracker` {list_age_hours, contradicted}. Suppliers map/list (web/src/components/SupplyMap.tsx) shows derived status with a quiet "List says … · Hamburg received …" line; do not touch Today.tsx/Launch.tsx/Routines.tsx (others own them); describe any UI you'd want there.
6. Tests for precedence, contradictions, feed freeze vs per-shipment silence, clock-based silence, cards appear only when it matters. Run `uv run pytest -q`, `uv run ruff check src tests --exclude tests/test_platform.py`, `cd web && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json`.
Report: what the real data now yields (which shipments get which derived status, which cards), files changed, risks.

site and uses their answer as the truth until the systems catch up.

A site question is {kind, subject, last_known (value, as_of, source), asked_at, token, answer}.

  replaces the book stock for that part.

to the site through the Teams channel and a push, with a link to /count/<token>: a phone page
that needs no dashboard password, only a valid token (random, stored here, expires at launch).

"""
Ask the floor: where Soony's systems lag behind the warehouse, an agent asks the people at the
site and uses their answer as the truth until the systems catch up.

A site question is {kind, subject, last_known (value, as_of, source), asked_at, token, answer}.
Three kinds, all found in the portal data at request time (nothing about Soony is written here):

- "packed": the packing count of a launch edition is older than ASK_PACKOUT_STALE_HOURS shift
  hours (only time inside packing windows counts), so Launch only projects at plan rate. Answer:
  copies packed now. A reported count newer than the log replaces the projection.
- "received": a shipment to the site is due (ETA passed, or at the port / out for delivery) and
  no goods receipt is booked for its order and part. Answer: arrived yes/no and how many. A "yes,
  N" counts as stock (reported, not booked) until a goods receipt appears.
- "count": a launch part whose book stock is what covers the plan (short, or less than
  ASK_COUNT_MARGIN headroom) was last counted ASK_COUNT_STALE_DAYS ago or before heavy use

  replaces the book stock for that part.

to the site through the Teams channel and a push, with a link to /count/<token>: a phone page
that needs no dashboard password, only a valid token (random, stored here, expires at launch).

"""
Paper check: read every supplier-side document in the portal and hold it against the ERP.

Suppliers and the DC write on paper (order confirmations, shipping advices, packing lists,
delivery notes, inspection reports, notices); SAP only knows what someone typed in. This agent
turns each document into claims, then runs small generic rules that look for a contradiction
between a claim and an ERP row. Every contradiction becomes an inbox card (findings.json,
decisions.json, impacts.json in the state folder) with both sides quoted, so nobody has to pick
one side silently.

1. Claims. Document text comes from the anchor index (PDF text layer, OCR for scans, table rows).
   Deterministic extraction first: references to known PO, goods receipt and delivery note
   numbers, table rows (item, part, description, quantity, price, currency, date), part lines
   with ordered / shipped / balance columns found by their header words, artwork revisions and
   status sentences (on hold, short shipment, lot does not meet AQL, ...). Then, when an OpenAI
   key is set, one LLM call per distinct free text (cached by content hash, so the same
   boilerplate on fifty confirmations costs one call) and one vision call per receiving scan whose
   goods receipt is still in stock (handwritten corrections). LLM statements are only kept when
   their quote is found in the document text.
2. Rules (see RULES): late or short delivery, old revision, receipt booked wrong, failed lot
   counted as stock, held at supplier.
3. Impact: remaining need per launch edition (day-one demand minus packed, times BOM usage)
   against stock plus open PO lines due before launch, with and without the contradicted
   quantity. A shortfall makes the card red; otherwise it is amber.

                        reply_at=at,

"""Packing clock: shifts from the plan workbook, night gaps skipped, packed = newest figure."""

from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import openpyxl

from ask_soony import launch

TZ = ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")


def make_portal(tmp_path, packed_status="60.300"):
    soony = tmp_path / "soony"
    (soony / "master").mkdir(parents=True)
    (soony / "context").mkdir()
    (soony / "erp").mkdir()
    (soony / "master" / "products.csv").write_text(
        "product_id,name,lifecycle,launch_date,day_one_qty\n"
        "P-A,Thing – Big Edition,launch,2030-06-02,1000\n"
        "P-OLD,Old,running,2020-01-01,\n"
    )
    wb = openpyxl.Workbook()
    ws = wb.active
    ws.title = "Editions"
    ws.append(["Plan · confidential"])
    ws.append(["Edition", "Product", "Day-one demand", "Packed", "Rate per hour"])
    ws.append(["Big", "P-A", 1000, 100, 50])
    sh = wb.create_sheet("Shifts")
    sh.append(["Day", "Shift", "Hours"])
    sh.append(["Saturday", "06:00–22:00", 16])
    sh.append(["Sunday", "06:00–20:00", 14])
    wb.save(soony / "context" / "launch_plan_X.xlsx")
    st = openpyxl.Workbook()
    fg = st.active
    fg.append(["Packed copies, later"])
    fg.append(["Site", "Material", "Qty"])
    fg.append(["DC", "P-A", packed_status])
    st.save(soony / "erp" / "stock_update_X.xlsx")
    return tmp_path


def test_windows_and_packed_from_any_source(tmp_path):
    clock = launch.load(make_portal(tmp_path, "400"), TZ)
    assert [(s.hour, e.hour) for s, e in clock.windows] == [(6, 22), (6, 20)]
    assert clock.windows[1][0].date().isoformat() == "2030-06-02"  # Sunday = launch day
    ed = clock.editions["P-A"]
    assert (ed.rate_per_hour, ed.packed, ed.remaining) == (50, 400, 600)


def test_line_never_stops_at_night(tmp_path):
    clock = launch.load(make_portal(tmp_path, "400"), TZ)
    sat_21 = datetime(2030, 6, 1, 21, 0, tzinfo=TZ)
    # 600 left at 50/h; 300 short -> 300 packable = 6 h: 1 h on Saturday, 5 h from Sunday 06:00
    stops = clock.line_stops(sat_21, "P-A", 300)
    assert stops == datetime(2030, 6, 2, 11, 0, tzinfo=TZ)
    # at night, nothing short is still fine, and slack counts only shift hours
    night = datetime(2030, 6, 2, 1, 0, tzinfo=TZ)
    assert clock.hours_left(night) == 14
    assert clock.slack_hours(night, "P-A") == 2.0
    assert clock.line_stops(night, "P-A", 0) is None
